title: ‘National disgrace’: Trump slams court ruling halting ballroom construction; to challenge in Supreme Court
content:
• A federal appeals court on Friday halted US President Donald Trump's plan to build a new 90,000-square-foot White House ballroom, ruling that congressional approval is required.
• The US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, in a 2-1 ruling, stated the President lacks unilateral authority for the proposed ballroom, which was planned for a capacity of 999 people.
• The Trump administration announced it would immediately appeal the federal appeals court's decision to the US Supreme Court, after the National Trust for Historic Preservation sued over the project in December last year.

title: Petrol, diesel prices today: Check fuel rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Kolkata as Crude oil weighs Iran-Oman deal
content:
• Indian retail petrol and diesel prices held steady on 8 August, with the last major price revision occurring over two months ago on 25 May.
• Brent crude, the global benchmark, climbed 1.3% to settle at $83.55 a barrel on Friday, while West Texas Intermediate crude fell 0.3% to $77.06 a barrel.
• Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey signed a joint defense agreement in Mecca on Friday, stipulating that an armed attack against any of the three would be regarded as an attack on all.

title: 'Homemade bombs and an AR-15:' How an American plotted to kill Lionel Messi during the FIFA World Cup
content:
• During the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) coordinated with the International Police Cooperation Center (IPCC), a joint security hub, to track terrorism alerts and threats.
• Argentine footballer Lionel Messi was a primary target during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, including a threat before the Argentina-Jordan match claiming "homemade bombs and an AR-15" would be used.
• French referee François Letexier received over six thousand threatening messages on his personal WhatsApp after his controversial performance in the Argentina-Egypt match during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

title: US-Iran war LIVE: US expects Iran-Oman deal on Hormuz soon; Saudi signs joint defense pact with Pakistan, Turkey
content:
• On Friday, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed a mutual defense agreement, establishing that an armed attack on one nation will be considered an attack against all three.
• The United States, on Friday, announced sanctions against six entities and one individual linked to Iran's illicit digital asset network, targeting two major digital asset exchanges and a network facilitating illicit activities.
• A US official on Friday reported progress in talks between Iran and Oman concerning the Strait of Hormuz, with Washington anticipating an agreement soon to restore oil and energy exports and potentially lift the naval blockade of Iranian ports.

title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke criticises Supreme Court’s comment on TMC MP Mahua Moitra’s ‘fear of eggs’
content:
• The Supreme Court, with a bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu, declined TMC MP Mahua Moitra's petition to appear virtually before the police.
• The Calcutta High Court had directed TMC MP Mahua Moitra to appear before investigators by August 14, after granting her interim protection.
• The Supreme Court questioned TMC MP Mahua Moitra's 'fear of eggs,' remarking, 'You are in politics and fear eggs? Freedom fighters took bullets.'

title: NEET paper leak masterminds used ‘FIFA World Cup 2026’ WhatsApp group: Secret chats play major role in CBI crackdown
content:
• The NEET UG paper leak led to the original examination on 12 May and a re-examination conducted on 21 June, culminating in Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.
• Manisha Mandhare created the "FIFA World Cup 2026" WhatsApp group in November 2025 to coordinate exam activities, and PV Kulkarni was identified and arrested on 15 May as the alleged mastermind.
• Manisha Sanjay Havaldar, a Physics expert, was arrested on 22 May for allegedly leaking 66 handwritten questions for monetary gain.

title: IP protection, FTA utilisation, contractual safeguards’ integration key for Indian exporters: Report
content:
• India aims to achieve a target of a $2 trillion export economy, advocating a shift in mindset from 'Make in India' to 'Own the World', as highlighted by Mohit Singla, chairman TPCI.
• Patent applications filed with the Indian Patent office increased significantly to 1.43 lakh in FY26 from 58,503 in FY21.
• Indian applicants accounted for 68,201 of the patent applications in 2024-25, representing approximately 62% of the total applications.

title: Onion, chicken prices make home-cooked meals costlier in July: Report
content:
• The cost of a vegetarian meal primarily rose due to a 20% jump in onion prices compared with a year ago, with onion prices surging 23% month-on-month in July.
• Broiler chicken prices climbed 14% year-on-year, accounting for nearly half the cost of a non-vegetarian meal, though they saw an estimated 2% decline month-on-month in July.
• Unseasonal rainfall and hailstorms in Maharashtra during March and April damaged the late-season onion crop and affected stored inventories, contributing to elevated onion prices.

title: India's forex reserves jump $10.5 billion to over two-month high of $692.87 billion as of July 31
content:
• India's forex reserves jumped by $10.5 billion to $692.87 billion as of July 31.
• India's foreign exchange reserves reached an all-time high of $728.494 billion in February this year.
• Foreign currency assets (FCAs), the largest component of the reserves, rose by $8.75 billion to $564.68 billion during the reporting week.

title: RBI allows gradual device restrictions for EMI defaults, eases recovery agent disclosure norms
content:
• Under new RBI norms, lenders cannot impose device restrictions until a loan is 30 days past due, can introduce graded restrictions between 30-60 days past due, and full restrictions only after 60 days past due.
• Lenders must pay compensation of ₹250 per hour, capped at the loan amount, if a borrower faces wrongful device restrictions or delay in restoring functionality, with restrictions to be reversed within one hour once dues are paid.
• The implementation date for the revised norms has been pushed to January 1, 2027 (from October 1, 2026), and lenders are now required to publish an updated list of engaged recovery agencies instead of detailed information about individual agents.
